executive_assessment.text: Named examples distinguish Shovi/Racha debris-flow impacts, drought-sensitive Kakheti, modeled regional poverty effects and human alterations to Poti's coastal sediment system.

Conflict-related displacement can deepen climate vulnerability through inadequate housing, restricted services and livelihood opportunities. This is a bounded reverse pathway, not evidence that climate caused Georgia's conflicts.
Reported municipal plans, basin mapping and monitoring systems are capacities and implementation outputs, not evaluated resilience or peace outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-11 reports: The CCDR records over 152 deaths and US$1.2 billion in losses from hazards over decades; landslides led to dozens of villages abandoned or displaced in 40 years. Shovi’s 2023 debris flow in Racha killed at least 32 and affected over 200.

Source dated 2025-11 reports: Among 100-year-flood-exposed people, 12% are poor and 77% have multiple vulnerabilities; among drought-exposed people, 12.1% are poor and 80% have multiple vulnerabilities. Kakheti is most drought-exposed; 91% there face other vulnerabilities.

The 2025 CCDR models higher food-price-related poverty under a dry/hot scenario than under stated policies, with particularly adverse consumption effects in Imereti, Mtskheta-Mtianeti, Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti and Kakheti. These are scenario results, not observed poverty changes.

Source dated 2025 reports: The UN analysis places spatial, social, political (including unresolved conflict) and environmental (including climate) factors among intersecting sources of vulnerability. Conflict disproportionately affects forcibly displaced people, residents outside government control and communities near Abkhazia/South Ossetia ABLs.

Source dated 2025-12 reports: By mid-century, heat risk covers Kvemo Kartli, Kakheti and the coast under SSP1-2.6, expanding across Kolkheti Plain under SSP3-7.0; mountainous areas face more days above 25°C under SSP3-7.0.
Source dated not stated reports: UNDP reports 150/154 planned weather stations in place; GECSA serves over 1,000 users in Kakheti and Shida Kartli, and landslide monitors are installed at 11 sites.

Source dated not stated reports: UNDP reports maps for seven hazards, vulnerability assessments and forecasting across 11 basins; the Emergency Management Service holds risk data, but public access awaits a protocol.

Source dated not stated reports: Emergency plans were adopted in six of 11 municipalities: Akhmeta, Gori, Kobuleti, Lagodekhi, Signagi and Telavi. Community plans cover 45 vulnerable western communities; measures are underway in 15 across Kintrishi, Natanebi and Supsa.

Source dated 2020-11 reports: The 2020 assessment says historic wetland drainage worsens lowland flood risk and is linked to coastal erosion, particularly around Poti; dams and port works also disrupt sediment delivery, including from Khobistskali, contributing to erosion and sediment accumulation at Poti port.

known_gaps.text: No inspected source directly linked active conflict or insecurity to interruption, delay or unequal delivery of climate adaptation in Georgia; broader political risks to sustainable development were not treated as an adaptation-specific reverse link.

The regional displacement source says much of Georgia has high IDP numbers but does not cross-tabulate Georgia-specific IDP locations with local climate hazards; it does not support assigning climate exposure to named conflict-affected settlements.

The UN report identifies people outside government control and communities near Abkhazia/South Ossetia ABL as conflict-affected, but the inspected sources provide limited climate-risk observations within those territories.
The water-use conflict projection names no tested institutional mediator or observed local dispute; no complete pathway is inferred from that warning.
The reverse pathway concerns conflict-related displacement and vulnerability, not demonstrated interruption of a particular adaptation project.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
